newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo dinar black mkt rate unchanged, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Yugo dinar black mkt rate unchanged, seen stable.

text.p: Yugoslavia's dinar, shaken by monetary expansion in last few days of 1996, traded on Thursday unchanged at 4.2 to the mark, street dealers said.
Economists and bankers expected the dinar rate to stabilise over next week but did not see the currency returning to its 3.4-3.5 level of before the November elections.
"It should stabilise around four to the German mark," one economist said.
Analysts said the central bank's monetary restrictiveness eased towards the end of 1996, with M1 money supply seen growing 10 percent over the last ten days of the year.
"There are indications that a lot more money -- around one billion dinars -- was put into circulation," said a top banking official who did not want to be named.
Slobodan Milosavljevic of the Institute for Market Research said the increase in money supply was an attempt by the debtors' lobby to shake the dinar and try to avoid paying back debts.
Analysts said the latest attack on the dinar was conducted with the help of some commercial banks.

Economists agreed the government will sooner or later have to acknowledge the changes in the dinar commercial rate. However they insisted a devaluation would be counterproductive before Yugoslavia restores ties with the International Monetary Fund and other financial institutions.
"Monetary authorities will have to devalue anyway once the membership in the IMF is obtained," Milosavljevic said.
Stojan Stamenkovic of the Institute of Economic Sciences (IEN) did not favour a change in the dinar official exchange rate at present. Instead, he suggested launching a crawling peg mechanism.

Another IEN economist Tomislav Popovic insisted the issue of devaluation will be ripe when unofficial hard currency reserves -- money held by Yugoslav banks and companies abroad -- are exhausted and no money is left to finance the country's swelling trade gap. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
